intent: Practice jumping by 5s from 0 to 20 to demonstrate that each number on the clock represents 5 minutes.

data.title: Time Traveler's Jump: Counting by Fives
data.description: Practice skip-counting by fives on a number line to understand how the minutes on a clock move forward.

challenges.instruction: Put your finger on the number 6, then make a big jump forward of 5 steps to the right.
challenges.hint: Follow the drawn arc on the number line and count 5 individual tick marks as you hop to the right.

challenges.instruction: Put your finger on 9, then make a big jump forward of 5 spaces to see where you land.
challenges.hint: Count 5 hops to the right one by one.

challenges.instruction: Put your finger on the number 1, and make a big jump forward of 5 steps to the right.
challenges.hint: Count 5 tick marks to the right from your starting spot.

challenges.instruction: Put your finger on 12 and make a big jump of 5 forward to see where you land.
challenges.hint: Count 5 tick marks to the right from 12.

judgement.reasoning: The obstacle is reading clock face numerals directly as minutes (e.g., pointing to 4 means :04 rather than :20). While the generator prompt asked to jump by 5s from 0 to 20, the generated content has students jumping by 5 from arbitrary starting numbers (6 to 11, 9 to 14, 1 to 6, 12 to 17), which fails to practice skip-counting multiples of 5 (5, 10, 15, 20) or mapping clock numbers to multiples of 5.
judgement.verdict: A teacher would not use this detour because jumping by 5 starting from 6, 9, or 12 does not help the student learn that clock numerals represent multiples of 5 minutes.
